test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which Indian naval asset participated in the defense exercise La Pérouse 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**INS Satpura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **INS Satpura** is an indigenously designed and built **Shivalik-class** guided-missile stealth frigate of the **Indian Navy**. It is known for its frequent participation in high-profile international maritime exercises, including **La Pérouse**.
 
• The exercise **La Pérouse** is a multilateral maritime drill led by the **French Navy** (**Marine Nationale**). It typically involves the participation of the **QUAD** nations, which includes **India**, the **United States of America**, **Japan**, and **Australia**.
 
• The participation of **INS Satpura** in the **2025** edition (projected in strategic maritime calendars) and previous editions like **2021** aims to enhance **interoperability**, maritime domain awareness, and tactical coordination among friendly foreign navies in the **Indo-Pacific** region.
 
• This naval asset was constructed at the **Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders Limited** (**MDL**) located in **Mumbai** and was officially commissioned into the **Indian Navy** on **20 August 2011**.
 
• As a multi-role frigate, **INS Satpura** is equipped with a versatile array of weapons and sensors, enabling it to perform **anti-air**, **anti-surface**, and **anti-submarine** warfare operations effectively during complex naval drills.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Exercise La Pérouse Origins:** The exercise is named after the **18th-century** French naval explorer **Jean-François de Galaup, comte de Lapérouse**. It serves as a platform for partner navies to demonstrate shared values in maintaining a **Free and Open Indo-Pacific**.
 
• **Technical Specifications:** **INS Satpura** has a displacement of approximately **6,200 tonnes** and a length of **143 meters**. It features advanced **stealth** technology that reduces its radar, infra-red, and magnetic signatures, making it difficult for enemy sensors to detect.
 
• **Weapon Systems:** The ship is armed with **BrahMos** supersonic cruise missiles, **Shtil-1** medium-range surface-to-air missiles, and **Club-N** anti-ship missiles. It also features a **76mm Super Rapid Gun Mount** (**SRGM**) for surface and aerial threats.
 
• **Aviation Capabilities:** To extend its surveillance and strike range, **INS Satpura** can carry two **HAL Dhruv** or **Westland Sea King** helicopters. These are utilized for **Search and Rescue** (**SAR**) and **Anti-Submarine Warfare** (**ASW**).
 
• **Operational Base:** The ship is a part of the **Eastern Fleet** of the **Indian Navy** and is based at **Visakhapatnam**, **Andhra Pradesh**. This strategic location allows it to maintain a persistent presence in the **Bay of Bengal** and the wider **Indian Ocean Region** (**IOR**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Multilateral Diplomacy:** Participation in **La Pérouse 2025** highlights **India’s** growing role as a **Net Security Provider** in the region. It showcases the capability of the **Indian Navy** to operate seamlessly with technologically advanced navies like the **US Navy** and the **French Navy**.
 
• **Evolution of Participation:** While **INS Satpura** participated in **2021**, other Indian vessels such as **INS Sahyadri** and the fleet tanker **INS Jyoti** took part in the **2023** edition, demonstrating the **Indian Navy’s** diverse asset deployment strategy.
 
• **Focus Areas:** The exercise focuses on advanced maritime maneuvers including **surface warfare**, **anti-air warfare**, **visit board search and seizure** (**VBSS**) operations, and **cross-deck helicopter flights**.
 
• **Strategic Impact:** Such exercises strengthen the **Security and Growth for All in the Region** (**SAGAR**) initiative promoted by the **Government of India**, fostering a rules-based international maritime order.
